body.estimand_functional: \(M_{ij}=E_P[Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]\).  With \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) as in \(\mathrm{def:loose\mbox{-}spectral\mbox{-}radius}\) and \(\widehat U^{\mathrm H}\) as in \(\mathrm{def:hybrid\mbox{-}estimator}\), \(c b_{nm}\le\inf_{\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}}\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}}E_P[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)]\le\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}}E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm H},U)]\le C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\) in the lower-bound regime, while \(\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)]\le Ca^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) remains the separate recorded-IPW guarantee.

sampling_model.design: A triangular array of sequential randomized decisions ordered globally by \(o(i,j)=(i-1)m+j\), with filtration \((\mathbb G_k)_{k=0}^{nm}\) and explicit row baselines \(\mathcal F_{i,0}=\mathbb G_{(i-1)m}\).
sampling_model.units: \(n\) units observed at \(m\) ordered decision times, with bounded aspect ratio; the sharp experiment and Markov witness use \(n_\ell=2\ell\) and \(m_\ell=2\lceil\gamma\ell\rceil\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary \(A_{ij}\) is drawn with \(p_{ij}\in[q,1-q]\) given the global pre-cell field \(\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Recorded IPW--SVD uses the known predictable propensities and requires no estimated treatment nuisance.  Its expected-risk guarantee follows from bounded matrix-martingale concentration and a deterministic singular-subspace bound.  The observed-data hybrid applies that fit only when the deterministic loose radius is at most one and otherwise reports the first \(r\) columns of the discrete-sine orthogonal matrix; its selector uses no unknown law feature.  The blind procedure replaces entrywise propensities by a clipped empirical row fraction, but in every nonempty fixed-complexity bounded-aspect regime its proved \(d_{nm}\) resolution is at least order \(\sqrt{\log n}\).  Simultaneous bands use direct recorded-IPW contrasts and deterministic variance envelopes; leave-one-cell-out residuals and multiplier studentization are not needed for the conservative theorem.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Published Theorem 1, equations (16b)--(17) on page 950, gives the rowwise upper bound, and Theorem 2, equation (22b) on page 953, gives the minimax lower bound under independent Bernoulli observation and independent noise.
Published Theorem 2.2 on page 1974 gives a Frobenius online-SGD rate and Theorem 3.1 on page 1977 gives fixed-form asymptotic normality for scalar rewards from independent Gaussian matrix contexts.
Published Theorem 3.1 and equations (17)--(18) on page 2389 bound nearest-neighbor error for each unit-by-time counterfactual mean under an adaptive pooled sequential policy.

Published Theorem 2 and equation (14) on page 1724 give a Frobenius RMSE upper bound for nuclear-norm completion of an untreated potential-outcome matrix when adoption dates are independent across units conditional on the latent matrix.

Published Theorem 3 in Section 4 of article e70002 gives a restricted-strong-convexity and Frobenius-error guarantee for the low-rank term estimated by the weighted MAR objective in equations (2) and (11).
Published Propositions 1--3 develop tall-wide factor imputation rates and limit laws for missing common components, with average and individual treatment effects on the treated as applications.

The published COLT extended abstract on pages 3821--3822 and its public full version give entrywise consistency and asymptotic normality for synthetic nearest neighbors under causal missing-not-at-random sampling.

Published Theorem 5 on page 2021 compares Frobenius upper bounds for known-propensity IPW and uniform-risk nuclear-norm completion under independent Bernoulli observation with a low-rank probability matrix.
The published article and its public full version develop groupwise nuclear-norm completion and debiased asymptotic normality for fixed block or staggered missing-not-at-random causal panels.

Public Theorem 3.2 and Corollary 3.3 give an armwise empirical-row-scaled SVD upper bound in matrix-row loss under armwise low-rank assumptions, with their own \(\log^4(n\vee m)\) factor.  Only the polynomial geometry \(\sqrt{n^{-1}+nm^{-2}}\) is shared with \(b^0_{nm}\); the present subspace scale \(b_{nm}\) additionally contains \(\sqrt{\log(en)}\) and the conversion factor \(B\sqrt{nm}/\lambda_{nm}\).
Published Theorem 3 and equation (10) on page 7 characterize variance improvement for a scalar adaptively normalized IPW estimator under independent treatment indicators.
Predictably weighted adaptive IPW scores yield scalar studentized martingale limits.
Balancing weights attain Frobenius guarantees and a lower bound under fixed heterogeneous missingness.
Debiased low-rank projection yields inference for a fixed linear form under independent sampling.

ArXiv Assumption 2 on pages 7--8 gives normalized third-moment, predictable-covariance, empirical-covariance, plug-in, growth, and variance-floor conditions under which Theorem 3.3 on page 8 validates simultaneous multiplier intervals for many martingale means.
Published Theorem 4 and equation (14) on page 348 validate a multiplier maximum for a coefficient matrix under modeled nonuniform missingness.

body.tldr: Recorded propensities identify the causal effect matrix and make the entrywise IPW errors a bounded row-major martingale-difference array.  In the stated small-\(b_{nm}\), signal-ceiling lower-bound regime, the strongest common-risk statement is now \(c b_{nm}\le\inf_{\widetilde U}\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)]\le\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm H},U)]\le C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\), where \(\widehat U^{\mathrm H}\) uses recorded IPW--SVD only when its loose radius is at most one and otherwise reports a deterministic discrete-sine frame.  Nonemptiness under bounded outcomes forces \(\lambda_{nm}\le2B\sqrt{nm}\); with fixed \(r,\mu,K,q\) and bounded aspect ratio this implies \(b_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n/n}\) and \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm},d_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n}\).  Thus the hybrid upper side is constant wherever the lower theorem applies, and the \(b_{nm}\)-to-constant minimax gap remains open there.  Recorded IPW--SVD still has its separate \(Ca^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) guarantee and its estimator-specific obstruction.  Blind row scaling is resolved only at the nonshrinking \(d_{nm}\) scale, the rank-one \(0.25/0.75\) Markov law remains its explicit HeartSteps II stress witness, and simultaneous dense-query bands retain a separate \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) entropy cost.

project_justification.gap: Published independent-mask rowwise matrix results do not settle causal effect-subspace risk under history-predictable assignment.  On the present bounded-outcome class, a constant-propensity packing yields the lower/reference scale \(b_{nm}\), while nonemptiness itself forces the loose spectral radius to be nonshrinking at fixed complexity.  The accepted endogenous-target example rules out uniform \(b_{nm}\)-attainment by recorded IPW--SVD only and supplies no estimator-independent converse above \(b_{nm}\).
project_justification.niche: The contribution is an explicit same-loss minimax bracket for a causal row subspace under predictable masks, now witnessed on the upper side by one observed-data hybrid with uniformly constant risk, together with a separate recorded-IPW guarantee, an estimator-specific obstruction, a calibrated blind-normalization resolution theorem, and conservative simultaneous causal-contrast bands whose entropy cost is separate.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the expected normalized maximum-row IPW bound, constructs a deterministic discrete-sine fallback with loss at most \(1+\sqrt{2/\mu}\), and combines them into a hybrid satisfying \(C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\).  Together with the constant-propensity Fano lower bound this yields the honest \(b_{nm}\)-to-constant minimax bracket under that theorem's small-\(b_{nm}\) and signal-ceiling conditions.  More generally, nonemptiness shows that the blind \(d_{nm}\) resolution is nonshrinking at fixed complexity and bounded aspect ratio.  The project also supplies the explicit Markov witness and retains direct finite-sample bands with separate family-size inflation.

body.related_work:
Mehrotra, Tran, Vu, and Zampetakis are the closest rowwise estimator comparator, but only the polynomial geometry \(\sqrt{n^{-1}+nm^{-2}}\) is shared.  Their public Theorem 3.2 and Corollary 3.3 have their own \(\log^4(n\vee m)\) factor, impose armwise conditions, and control matrix-row loss.  The present \(b_{nm}\) additionally contains \(\sqrt{\log(en)}\) and the subspace-conversion factor \(B\sqrt{nm}/\lambda_{nm}\).  Algebraically, for arm-mean matrices \(\mathsf M^0,\mathsf M^1\), \(\operatorname{rank}(\mathsf M^1-\mathsf M^0)\le\operatorname{rank}(\mathsf M^1)+\operatorname{rank}(\mathsf M^0)\).  The converse fails: a bounded full-rank common component \(C\) and a bounded low-rank perturbation \(\Delta\) can be chosen so that \(C+\Delta\) remains full rank, giving \(\mathsf M^0=C\), \(\mathsf M^1=C+\Delta\), and low-rank effect \(\Delta\).  This algebra yields neither full-class containment nor rate transfer.

Cai, Li, Chi, Poor, and Chen prove two-to-infinity upper and lower bounds for an independently sampled low-rank matrix with independent noise; those results inform the deterministic perturbation and local packing architecture but do not make the causal target predictable under the row-major filtration.  Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey support the recorded-propensity martingale-score reduction, and Tropp supplies the bounded-increment matrix Freedman inequality.  Dwivedi, Tian, Tomkins, Klasnja, Murphy, and Shah study adaptive nearest-neighbor estimation of unit-by-time arm means under an exogenous factor model, a different target and structural class.  Athey, Bayati, Doudchenko, Imbens, and Khosravi; Sun, Zhu, and Dubin; Bai and Ng; Agarwal, Dahleh, Shah, and Shen; Choi and Yuan; Mao, Wong, and Chen; and Wang, Wong, Mao, and Chan address outcome completion, treatment effects on treated cells, entrywise or Frobenius loss, or fixed missingness structures.  None closes the present estimator-independent \(b_{nm}\)-to-constant gap.

Khan and Ugander analyze scalar affine normalization under independent indicators; the blind row-fraction SVD and its \(0.25/0.75\) Markov witness are new objects here and do not refute that published procedure.  Belloni and Oliveira and Ma, Niu, Zhang, and Zhu motivate high-dimensional martingale or multiplier inference, but the retained simultaneous theorem uses direct finite-sample Freedman radii and a union bound only.  Its \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) factor is a query-family entropy cost, not part of either subspace scale.  Spruijt-Metz et al. make saved propensities and omission sensitivity operationally relevant for the HeartSteps II consumer.

body.technical_internal_limitation: Bounded outcomes and the signal-floor assumption imply \(\lambda_{nm}\le2B\sqrt{nm}\) whenever the class is nonempty.  Consequently, with fixed \(r,\mu,K,q\) and bounded aspect ratio, \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) and \(d_{nm}\) are at least order \(\sqrt{\log n}\); neither is a shrinking uniform resolution.  The discrete-sine hybrid converts the former into a valid constant upper risk, but no observed-data construction is known to achieve the lower/reference scale \(b_{nm}\), and no estimator-independent converse larger than \(b_{nm}\) is proved.  The frozen class permits target singular factors to depend on earlier outcomes, so ordinary leave-one-row arguments cannot treat those factors as predictable; the explicit obstruction makes this substantive for recorded IPW--SVD.  For blind normalization, separate arm means enter the denominator derivative and are not estimable at a claimed frontier rate under the effect-only low-rank assumptions.  No residual covariance consistency, positive random studentizer, or feasible multiplier exactness is assumed or claimed.
body.honest_scope: Identification is given by the recorded-IPW conditional mean.  Under the lower theorem's small-\(b_{nm}\) and signal-ceiling conditions, the proved statistical headline is the expected-risk bracket between the lower/reference scale \(b_{nm}\) and the constant-risk observed-data hybrid \(\widehat U^{\mathrm H}\).  More generally, in every nonempty fixed-complexity bounded-aspect regime, the available IPW and blind radii are nonshrinking, so neither supplies a matched rate.  The adaptive endogenous-target construction refutes only uniform \(b_{nm}\)-attainment by recorded IPW--SVD; it does not show that every estimator measurable from \(A,Y,p\) fails at that scale.  Minimax tightness must be settled before a finite sharp constant is meaningful.  The blind procedure is certified only at \(d_{nm}\), and the \(0.25/0.75\) Markov sequence is a boundary example for that procedure and a HeartSteps II stress design, not a refutation of a published method.  Simultaneous inference is supplied by conservative finite-sample direct-IPW radii with separate \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) inflation, not by feasible multiplier exactness.
